newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Westpac leads note issue for BNP.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Westpac leads note issue for BNP.

text.p: Westpac Banking Corp said it had lead managed an A$150 million fixed rate note issue for Banque Nationale de Paris' Australian branch.

The notes, which mature April 2000, pay a 6.5 percent coupon and were priced at a 25 basis points spread over the Australian Treasury April 2000 bond on Tuesday. The issue carries BNP's global rating of A plus from Standard & Poor's.

"The fact that a major international bank like BNP is issuing so early in the new year reflects the growing maturity and depth of the market," said Micheal Hawker, Head of Financial Markets, Westpac Institutional & International Banking Group.
The notes were issued under a domestic medium term note programme arranged by Westpac, which are also dealers with BNP on the programme.
The BNP issue represents the first of what Westpac believes is shaping up to be an important year for Australia's domestic corporate market.

"As far as we are concerned, the debate about the domestic bond market is obsolete - the market is here and on our analysis it is here to stay," Hawker said, adding that he expected to see a significant number of issuers accessing the market.
Denis Fountain, Assistant General Manager Capital Markets at BNP, said the past six months had seen growing investor interest in non-government issues and a concomitant contraction in credit spreads.
"This had allowed an issue to be brought to the domestic market which was a good fit for BNP in terms of the liquidity and maturity profile," he added.
